subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`, its `node-pty` install-script dependency, packaged native executables, and argv-carried base64 config boundary for this prerelease external sandbox plugin after the stray export is removed?
rationale: The code cleanup is mechanical, but accepting a first-party sandbox backend backed by native preview tooling and config-on-argv behavior is a repository security-boundary decision that automation cannot make.

options.title: Accept After Export Cleanup
options.body: Remove the stray sandbox barrel export, then have admin/secops approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC argv boundary.

options.title: Pause For Safer Transport
options.body: Keep the PR open until upstream MXC provides a non-argv config transport or OpenClaw documents a stricter accepted boundary.

options.title: Decline First-Party Ownership
options.body: Move this out of the OpenClaw repo path if maintainers do not want to own this native sandbox dependency surface as an official plugin.

recommendation.title: Accept After Export Cleanup
recommendation.body: Remove the stray sandbox barrel export, then have admin/secops approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC argv boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned and has recent sandbox/plugin SDK history on the exact boundary affected by the remaining cleanup and decision.
